about: print12: the print series of the book (6 x 9 in, standard color, print on demand). series_title is THE ONE PLACE the series (and the online book) is named: tools/book/build_series.py uses it for the covers, title pages, running heads, copyright pages and the /book/ series block, and tools/book/build_book.py for the online book, its packages and PDFs. Change it, then rebuild (build_book.py, build_pdfs.js, build_series.py, BOOK_SERIES=1 build_pdfs.js). Chapters are the short versions, in the order given here. The paperbacks use free KDP ISBNs, so no ISBN is printed (see "isbn"). The imprint is "Independently published". summary_at_end: chapters that print "What to remember" at the end in place of "In short" at the top (never both). examples: false leaves the filled-in examples out of the print books.

price_rule.about: The owner's pricing rule for every paperback: fewer than short_under_pages printed pages is the short line at short_usd, anything longer is regular_usd. tools/book/build_pdfs.js applies it to the final page count (so it overrides the price_usd values above, which are only the expected results), writes list_price into book/print/series.json, and listing_kdp.py and kdp_steps.py read it from there.

books.title: Know Yourself Kindly
books.sub: Where your lens came from, who you are now, and who you are becoming
books.line: Start with yourself: your history, your wiring, your feelings, your worth and how your mind works.
books.blurb: Before you can share a life well, it helps to know your own. This warm book starts with you. Where did your way of seeing things come from: the home you grew up in, the old rules, the things life taught you? How are you wired today: your energy, your weather, the words that land and the ones that sting? And who are you becoming, one small step at a time? Along the way it explains how feelings work, why your worth is not a score, why personality is more like a set of sliders than a box, and how minds work differently, from ADHD and autism to sensory and learning differences, with ways to meet in the middle. Every chapter has everyday scenes, words you could use and one small thing to try this week. Nothing here is a test. Read it on your own, at your own pace.

books.title: Heal and Steady
books.sub: Stress, anger, worry, loss and repair, and finding your footing again
books.line: For the heavy days: stress, anger, worry and low mood, grief, repair, change and what matters to you.
books.blurb: Some days are heavy. Stress piles up, anger flares, worry keeps you awake, or a loss changes everything. This book is about steadying yourself through all of it, gently and without blame. It explains what stress does to the body and why it adds up, what anger is for and what helps in the hot minutes, and how worry, low mood and trauma work. It walks with you through grief in its many forms, through repair and apologies that land, and through the slow work of change, one small step at a time. It ends with what matters to you, and what a good life can mean. Each chapter has words you could use and one small thing to try. Go at your own pace.

books.title: Understanding Each Other
books.sub: How we hear, see and belong to each other, at home and in every group
books.line: Pace and tone, how words land, how we see each other, belonging, love, groups and helping well.
books.blurb: Two people can care about each other and still fall out of tune. One wants to talk now, and the other needs an hour. A comment meant lightly lands hard. This book is about understanding the people around you: at home, in families, with friends, at work and in every group you belong to. It explains how pace and tone pull people apart, how communication really works, and why two people can see the same moment so differently. It looks at why we need to belong, how trust grows and is rebuilt, how love takes many forms, and the quiet pull of the groups we are part of. It ends with helping others well, with kind limits and without burning out. Each chapter has everyday scenes, words you could use and one small thing to try. No blame and no verdicts: just a clearer view and a kinder next step.

books.title: Share the Load
books.sub: The work nobody sees, and a fair, kind way to share it
books.line: For homes, families and teams: seeing the unseen work, one owner per job, and two kinds of fair.
books.blurb: Every shared home, family or team runs on work that nobody sees: noticing the shoes are too small, booking the appointment, remembering trash day. When that work isn’t counted, someone ends up carrying more than anyone realizes, and resentment grows quietly. This book helps you see the whole load, kindly and without keeping score. It shows a simple way to check whether the way you share the work can last, how much of a reaction is leftover stress, how to agree what fair means to each of you, and a gentle monthly look-back that catches what weekly chats miss. Each chapter points to a workpaper that puts it to use, free to print from the website. It ends with an afterword that draws the threads of the whole series together. It looks at the setup, never at the person.

workbook.title: The Workpapers: The Bound Edition
workbook.sub: Every form from the series in one book, on big pages, with room to write
workbook.line: Every workpaper from the series in one bound book, with spare copies and the math on paper.
workbook.blurb: Every workpaper from the Spread Love & Acceptance books is free to print or fill out on screen at spreadloveandacceptance.com. This is the bound edition, for anyone who would rather have them all in one place, on big pages, with a pencil. Inside are blank copies of all ten: a quick check of how much you’re carrying, a calm-down plan you make on a calm day, a self-check before you reply to something that stung, a 90-second daily check-in, a one-week log of who did what, a monthly look-back and more, plus a paper version of the setup score. Each one starts with a short page on when to use it, how long it takes and which book explains it. Then come spare copies, a six-week planner and pages for your own notes. The sheets describe what happened, never who someone is.

isbn.how: voice18 (owner): every paperback uses a free KDP ISBN, chosen on KDP's Paperback Content screen ("Get a free KDP ISBN"). KDP prints it in the barcode, so the copyright pages carry no ISBN line, and the imprint is KDP's "Independently published". Kindle editions and the box set need no ISBN (Amazon gives them an ASIN). Leave these values empty; they are kept only so a future edition could record the ISBNs KDP assigns.
